items.label: f05-swap-lowest-match
items.front: Portal: the button labelled 'Swap lowest match' sets `swapTarget = selectedItems[selectedItems.length - 1]` (src/App.jsx:210, 259-262). What does a subscriber actually get?
items.back: The LAST item in the box is swapped, whatever its score - a high-match item can be thrown out while a poor match stays. Fix: choose the selected item with the minimum scoreItem(...) and add a unit test that pins the label's promise.

items.label: f01-reserve-not-idempotent
items.front: Curator dashboard: 'Reserve SKUs' maps every boxed item to `Math.max(0, stock - 1842)` and keeps no record that this cycle was already reserved (src/App.jsx:500-504). What is the risk, and what is the fix?
items.back: Repeated clicks or retries over-reserve stock, and the clamp hides shortfalls. Fix: a cycle-scoped reservation command with an idempotency key (e.g. reserve_inventory:cycle=2026-06) that rejects or no-ops a repeat and flags insufficient stock.

items.label: f02-failed-payment-ledger
items.front: Billing: failPayment adds `plan.price` to `subscriber.balance` on every call, with no invoice id (src/App.jsx:316-323). What does a duplicate failure event do, and what is the fix?
items.back: Each duplicate failure inflates the open balance by another full invoice, corrupting the ledger. Fix: an invoice-state model - the balance is derived from invoices, and a failure transitions one invoice (idempotently) instead of adding money.

items.label: f04-dunning-only-logs
items.front: Billing: the 'Send dunning' button only calls addEvent('Dunning email sent', ...) - there is no network call or queue (src/App.jsx:375-381). What operational risk does this create, and what is the production fix?
items.back: The timeline claims an email went out when nothing was sent - false operational confidence. Fix: write an outbox row in the same transaction as the billing change and let a worker deliver it with retry and dedupe; log 'sent' only on delivery.

items.label: f03-duplicate-shipments
items.front: Fulfillment: the month-start job prepends a shipment with a `Math.random()` id and never checks whether this subscriber already has one for the cycle (src/App.jsx:557-568). A cron fires twice. Consequence and fix?
items.back: The subscriber gets two boxes for one paid cycle, and random ids make it untestable. Fix: a unique constraint on (subscriber_id, cycle_month), a retry-safe job that upserts, and injected id providers for tests.

items.prompt: A teammate proposes moving changePlan behind `POST /subscription/change-plan` that accepts `{ planId, price, proration }` from the browser. What is the blocking review comment?

choices.text: Price and proration are money authority: the server must load the plan price by id itself, or any client can submit its own amount
Only proration must move server-side; plan prices are public, so trusting them is fine
None: HTTPS already prevents the client from altering the request body
It is safe as long as the endpoint also logs a timeline event for auditing

choices: Price and proration are money authority: the server must load the plan price by id itself, or any client can submit its own amount
Only proration must move server-side; plan prices are public, so trusting them is fine
None: HTTPS already prevents the client from altering the request body
It is safe as long as the endpoint also logs a timeline event for auditing

items.explanation: Client-side prices cannot be trusted for billing; send only planId, compute server-side, and reconcile against provider webhooks.

items.prompt: After one failed invoice the subscriber is past_due. The admin keeps clicking 'Retry charge'. When does the payment recover, and why is that a design smell?

choices.text: On the second retry click, because recovery is keyed on a local counter reaching 2 rather than on any payment-provider result
Never: retries only escalate the dunning stage until a new card is saved
On the first retry click, since any retry clears the past_due flag
On the third retry click, once the firm-email dunning stage has finished

Never: retries only escalate the dunning stage until a new card is saved
On the first retry click, since any retry clears the past_due flag
On the third retry click, once the firm-email dunning stage has finished

items.explanation: failPayment sets retryAttempt to 1; the first retry bumps it to 2, the second sees `retryAttempt >= 2` and zeroes the balance. Real retry state should come from provider events.

A validation error, because a proration of zero is rejected

items.explanation: The guide notes 'Same selected plan can be clicked.' changePlan has no guard and labels every `delta <= 0` as a downgrade credit.

items.prompt: A curator clicks 'Reserve SKUs' twice for the same June box. What happens to the stock of the boxed items?

choices.text: React batches both clicks into a single update, so stock only drops once
Each click subtracts the full 1,842-unit reservation again, so the same cycle is reserved twice
The second click is a no-op because those item ids are already marked reserved
The second click throws because the subtraction would push stock below zero

items.explanation: reserveInventory maps every boxed item to `stock - 1842` with no record of which cycle was already reserved: the operation is not idempotent.

items.prompt: On the Billing tab the admin clicks 'Fail invoice' two times in a row for the same invoice. What does the ledger show?

choices.text: The open balance grows by another full plan price on each click, as if two separate invoices had failed
The balance is overwritten with the plan price, so it still reflects one invoice
The second click is ignored because paymentHealth is already past_due
retryAttempt resets to 0 and the open balance is left unchanged

choices: The open balance grows by another full plan price on each click, as if two separate invoices had failed
The balance is overwritten with the plan price, so it still reflects one invoice
The second click is ignored because paymentHealth is already past_due
retryAttempt resets to 0 and the open balance is left unchanged

items.explanation: failPayment does `balance: current.balance + plan.price` unconditionally; there is no invoice entity whose state could make a repeated failure a no-op.

items.prompt: itm_101 has 420 units in stock and reserveInventory computes `Math.max(0, item.stock - 1842)`. What real problem does the clamp hide?

choices.text: About 1,422 subscribers get no reserved unit, yet the catalog just shows 0 and the shortfall is recorded nowhere
Nothing: showing 0 units correctly means every box received one
Stock becomes -1422, which crashes the inventory catalog when it renders
The clamp rejects the whole reservation and leaves the stock at 420

Nothing: showing 0 units correctly means every box received one

The clamp rejects the whole reservation and leaves the stock at 420

items.explanation: The guide's invariant is 'Stock reservation must not go negative' - but clamping is not enforcing it, it silently discards the over-reservation instead of failing or flagging it.

choices.text: The second event overwrites the first, because events are stored in an object keyed by id
They share an id, so React sees duplicate keys in the timeline and tests cannot predict event ids
Nothing: Date.now() returns a strictly increasing value on every call
The timeline sorts by id and shows the two events in reverse order

items.explanation: Date.now() has millisecond resolution and is not unique per call; the guide calls it 'convenient but not collision-proof' and suggests injecting id/time providers.

items.prompt: Maya has excluded 'Lavender'. Why could an item tagged Lavender still rank near the top of her recommendation queue?

choices.text: scoreItem never reads preferences.excluded; only the Preferences screen uses that list
scoreInventory filters it out, but the queue renders the unscored inventory instead
The 12-point floor in Math.max lifts every excluded item back to the top
Exclusion only subtracts 35 points; enough tag matches, a good rating and novelty can still outscore other items

items.explanation: `blocked ? 35 : 0` is a penalty, not a filter. Hard exclusion must be enforced before selection, not only in display (review kata 7).

items.prompt: toggleSkip flips skipNext with a functional updater but chooses the timeline text from `subscriber.skipNext`. When can the logged text disagree with the resulting state?

choices.text: Always, because addEvent runs first and therefore describes the previous state
When two toggles run before a re-render: both read the same render-time value, so both log the same message while the state flips twice
Never, because the functional updater runs synchronously before addEvent reads the value
Only after a reload, because skipNext is restored from storage with the old value

items.explanation: The updater sees the latest queued state, but the closure's `subscriber` is fixed for that render - the classic stale-closure split between state and side-effect copy.

Two June shipments for the same subscriber, each with a different random id, because nothing checks subscriber plus cycle uniqueness
The second run replaces the first, since both rows carry the same subscriber name

items.prompt: You must make the month-start shipment job safe to run twice. Which idempotency key works?

choices.text: A key scoped to the subscriber and the billing cycle, such as subscriber sub_4289 plus cycle 2026-06
The timestamp at which the job started, so each run is uniquely tagged
The generated shipment id, such as shp_4821, since it already identifies the row
The plan name combined with the destination city of the shipment

choices: A key scoped to the subscriber and the billing cycle, such as subscriber sub_4289 plus cycle 2026-06
The timestamp at which the job started, so each run is uniquely tagged
The generated shipment id, such as shp_4821, since it already identifies the row
The plan name combined with the destination city of the shipment

items.explanation: Idempotency means a second run with the same key has the same effect as one run; only the business identity (who, which cycle) is stable across retries - generated ids and timestamps differ on every run.

items.prompt: scoredItems is memoized on [inventory, subscriber.preferences, ratings]. What breaks if `ratings` is removed from that dependency list?

choices.text: New star ratings update state, but the queue keeps the scores computed from old ratings until preferences or inventory change
The memo reads ratings through its closure, so it sees new ratings automatically
Nothing, because useMemo recomputes on every render regardless of its list
React throws a missing-dependency error at runtime and the tab fails to render

choices: New star ratings update state, but the queue keeps the scores computed from old ratings until preferences or inventory change
The memo reads ratings through its closure, so it sees new ratings automatically
Nothing, because useMemo recomputes on every render regardless of its list
React throws a missing-dependency error at runtime and the tab fails to render

items.explanation: useMemo only recomputes when a listed dependency changes identity; rateItem replaces the ratings array, which is exactly the signal the memo would miss. 'Missing dependency in useMemo creates stale results.'
